The business under the new price: growth keeps getting faster

Databricks reported $6.9 billion in annualized revenue in June, up 80% year over year, and July's announcement added nothing to those numbers.[7] What the announcement re-priced is a growth rate that has climbed at every disclosure: the company reported $4.0 billion last September, $4.8 billion in December, $5.4 billion in February, and $6.9 billion in June. Software companies at this scale usually slow down. Databricks keeps speeding up.

Composition explains part of the acceleration. The AI product line reached $1.7 billion in annualized revenue by June, up from $1.4 billion in February, and the data-warehousing product that competes directly with Snowflake crossed $1.5 billion, doubling year over year.[6][7] Growth of that kind arrives with a bill attached. Gross margin fell to 74% from above 80%, and management expects further declines because AI agents run queries at machine speed while the computing bill lands in cost of revenue.[7] For our quality score, 70% is the line that matters; below it, we rebuild the score regardless of what the round does. The cushion today is four percentage points.

The rest of the operating picture is strong but stale. February's disclosure showed positive free cash flow, net revenue retention above 140%, and more than 20,000 customer organizations; those figures are now six months old, and we weight them accordingly.[6] Headcount stood at 9,000 in June.[5] The next update, expected between September and October, refreshes everything at once, which concentrates a quarter's worth of evidence into a single window.
